title: Agent Chat: tool-policy / confirmation layer for destructive ops in the autonomous loop
description:
SAFETY follow-up surfaced by QA of Agent Chat P3 (commit 5c55eaa, task 1278). P3 wires the OpenRouter LLM into a LIVE multi-step AI SDK v6 loop (runAgentTurn -> streamText, stopWhen stepCountIs(24), abortSignal) that AUTO-EXECUTES the full P2 tool set. buildAgentTools() (packages/authoring-ui/src/agentchat/tools.ts) iterates ALL_COMMANDS with NO filtering, so every destructive / side-effecting command is a live, auto-running tool the model can call without any confirmation: stage_remove, library_remove, timeline_remove_layer, timeline_remove_frame, scene_remove, doc_load (full document replace), file_save_fla, file_load_fla, publish_swf. The autonomous loop can chain up to 24 steps and freely delete/overwrite/replace the document with zero user confirmation, allowlist, dry-run, or per-tool gating. The only mitigations today: (a) all model mutations go through pushDoc so they are undoable via history_undo, and (b) file ops are in-memory. The system prompt (systemPrompt.ts) mentions undo but adds no guard.

JUDGMENT: for an interactive user-driven chat where the user watches and can undo, the current posture is arguably acceptable; but an AUTONOMOUS multi-step loop executing destructive ops with zero confirmation is a legitimate medium-severity risk now that it is reachable (P2 watch-item, now live in P3). doc_load / file_load_fla full-replace and publish_swf are the worst cases (a full-replace is one undo entry but can blow away substantial work; publish has external side effects).

RECOMMEND a lightweight tool-policy layer: classify commands as read-only vs mutating vs destructive (the agent-protocol registry already knows each command's effect); for the destructive class, either (1) require a per-call user confirmation chip in the chat before execute() runs, or (2) gate behind an opt-in 'allow destructive ops' toggle in AgentSettings (default off), or (3) a read-only/dry-run mode. Confirmation chips are the most Flash-authoring-friendly. Out of scope for this task: nothing else in the loop is broken — runaway guard (stepCountIs(24)), graceful structured tool-error handling (AgentToolError, never throws past the loop), streaming, and AbortController Stop are all present and correct (verified by QA + 15 agentLoop unit tests). This task is ONLY the destructive-op guard. Scope: tools.ts tool-policy classification + AgentChatPanel confirmation UI (or settings toggle); add unit tests asserting destructive tools require confirmation/are gated.
